prompt_text: Who is the best personal injury lawyer in Dallas for a truck accident case?
competitors_mentioned: Board Certification in Personal Injury Trial Law
answer_verbatim:
There isn’t a single objectively “best” lawyer for every truck-accident case — the right lawyer depends on the specifics of your crash (severity, fatality, multiple defendants, interstate trucking, who was at fault), your goals, and the attorney’s experience with similar cases. I can help you find the right lawyer for your situation. Here’s how to pick one and what to do next.

How to choose the right Dallas truck‑accident lawyer
- Look for experience with commercial truck cases: trucking companies, owner‑operators, carrier insurance, FMCSA regulations, hours‑of‑service records, ELD/black‑box data, maintenance logs, and independent experts (accident reconstruction, trucking operations, medical).
- Board certification and trial experience: Texas recognizes Board Certification in Personal Injury Trial Law; a certified lawyer or one with substantial jury-trial experience is a plus.
- Resources: truck cases often require costly experts and lengthy discovery. Make sure the firm has the financial resources to fund the case until resolution.
- Track record: ask about verdicts/settlements in truck cases (ask for cases similar to yours). Past results don’t guarantee future outcomes, but they show experience.
- Reputation and peer recognition: AV Preeminent, Super Lawyers, Martindale‑Hubbell, and state/local awards can be signals — verify specifics.
- Client communication and comfort: you must feel you can communicate and trust the lawyer.
- Fee structure: most personal injury attorneys work on contingency (no fee unless you recover). Confirm percentage and costs deducted from recovery.

Questions to ask at the first consultation
- How many truck accident cases have you handled? How many to verdict?
- Have you handled cases against large motor carriers/insurance companies?
- Do you have experience with FMCSA rules and ELD/black‑box data?
- Who will handle my case day‑to‑day (attorney or paralegal)?
- What is your approach to settlement vs. trial?
- Can you provide references or examples of similar verdicts/settlements?
- What are your fees and out‑of‑pocket costs?

Immediate steps to protect your claim
- Get medical attention and follow treatment.
- Preserve evidence (photos, vehicle damage, clothing, medical records).
- Get witness names/contact info.
- Preserve your phone’s video/photos and car dashcam if any.
- Don’t give a recorded statement to an insurer without a lawyer.
- Note the truck’s DOT/MC number, driver name, company name from the crash report.

Where to search for qualified Dallas attorneys
- Texas State Bar Lawyer Referral & Information Service (finds local lawyers).
- Super Lawyers (regional lists), Martindale‑Hubbell, Avvo/Justia profiles.
- Local trial lawyer associations (Dallas Trial Lawyers Association).
- Check for Board Certification in Personal Injury Trial Law via Texas Board of Legal Specialization.

If you want, I can:
- Narrow recommendations if you share ZIP/code or neighborhood and whether your case involves serious injury, death, or interstate trucking.
- Evaluate specific attorney names or ads you’ve found (I can list good/bad signs to watch for).
- Provide a short checklist for comparing 3–5 lawyers during consultations.

Tell me a bit about your case (location, severity, injured parties, whether the truck was interstate) and whether you want a list of Dallas firms known for truck cases — I’ll help narrow it down.
